page.layout: One page of text: running head across the top; a title heading with emblem number; an engraving (woodcut) in the middle; the verse epigram and motto below the picture; a closing line "Equus" at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.head: Globus, è nubibus, tenui filo, quod Dei manus tenet, suspensus, Ecclesiam designans. IX.
main_text.p: [Engraving: a walled city on a globe suspended by a thread from a hand emerging from clouds, over a landscape.]
Pinge globum tenui quem libratum Vndique filo.

p.i: Talis es Vrbs Christi de nomine dicto beato,
Qua nil firmius est, mobiliúsque nihil.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a walled city with towers on a sphere hung from a hand in clouds, above a rocky landscape; described, not transcribed. The initial P of the verse is a large decorative letter. The word "Equus" at the foot is printed in larger type and may be a catchword or signature-like element; left as a paragraph. Ligature forms "Vndique", "Suftineat" and "Talis" are read as printed.
